001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul.logmanager;
002
003import java.util.Collections;
004import java.util.Enumeration;
005import java.util.HashSet;
006import java.util.Map;
007import java.util.Set;
008import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap;
009import java.util.logging.LogManager;
010import java.util.logging.Logger;
011
012/**
013 * A {@link LogManager} implementation that vends {@link RainbowGumJULLogger}s, routing
014 * every {@code java.util.logging.Logger} call directly through Rainbow Gum instead of the
015 * normal Handler/Level dispatch. Modeled closely on
016 * {@code org.apache.logging.log4j.jul.LogManager} (log4j-jul), including its guard
017 * against reentrant {@link #getLogger(String)} calls.
018 * <p>
019 * <strong>Installation is a JVM-wide, one-shot decision made before this class is even
020 * loaded.</strong> Set the system property {@code java.util.logging.manager} to this
021 * class's fully qualified name, as a real {@code -D} JVM argument (or via
022 * {@code JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS}), before any code in the JVM touches
023 * {@code java.util.logging}:
024 * <pre>{@code java.util.logging.manager=io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul.logmanager.RainbowGumLogManager}</pre>
025 * {@link LogManager#getLogManager()} resolves this property exactly once, via a static
026 * bootstrap, so calling {@link System#setProperty(String, String)} after the JVM has
027 * started is too late; see this class's own package for why that forces this module's own
028 * tests into dedicated, non-reused-fork JVMs.
029 * <p>
030 * <b>GraalVM native image</b>: this module bundles a {@code native-image.properties} (at
031 * {@code META-INF/native-image/io.jstach.rainbowgum/rainbowgum-jul-logmanager/}) with
032 * {@code -Djava.util.logging.manager=...} plus a matching
033 * {@code --initialize-at-build-time=io.jstach.rainbowgum.jul.logmanager.RainbowGumLogManager}
034 * as native-image build arguments - the same technique <a href=
035 * "https://github.com/helidon-io/helidon/blob/main/logging/log4j/src/main/resources/META-INF/native-image/io.helidon.logging/helidon-logging-log4j/native-image.properties">Helidon's
036 * own {@code helidon-logging-log4j} module uses</a> for its equivalent
037 * {@code LogManager}. Baking the property into the build lets {@code LogManager}'s static
038 * bootstrap run once, during the build itself in a real JDK environment, so the
039 * fully-initialized {@code RainbowGumLogManager} instance ends up frozen directly into
040 * the image heap with nothing left to resolve at startup - verified with a real GraalVM
041 * build, the resulting executable needs no runtime argument at all, not even the
042 * {@code -D} above. The {@code --initialize-at-build-time} half is not optional: without
043 * it, native-image's own build-time-heap-safety analysis refuses to embed a
044 * {@code RainbowGumLogManager} instance whose type was not itself explicitly marked for
045 * build-time initialization, even though the instance was already legitimately
046 * constructed during the build.
047 * <p>
048 * An earlier attempt deferred {@code java.util.logging} initialization to runtime instead
049 * ({@code --initialize-at-run-time=java.util.logging}) so the system property above could
050 * be passed at native-image runtime exactly like on a normal JVM - that works, but costs
051 * two runtime {@code -D} arguments instead of zero: a native-image executable has no JDK
052 * installation directory behind it, and {@code LogManager}'s
053 * primordial-configuration-file lookup throws {@code Error: Can't find java.home ??}
054 * unconditionally once it actually runs at startup, regardless of whether a custom
055 * {@code LogManager} is even in play - {@code -Djava.home=} <i>anything non-null</i>
056 * would also have been required alongside the property above, for every consumer,
057 * forever. Baking the property into the build avoids that problem entirely, since the
058 * primordial-lookup code path it triggers never runs at native-image startup at all with
059 * this approach.
060 *
061 * @see RainbowGumJULLogger
062 */
063public final class RainbowGumLogManager extends LogManager {
064
065        private final Map<String, Logger> loggers = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
066
067        // Guards against a Logger vended by this LogManager (or something Rainbow Gum
068        // itself does while resolving a route) triggering a reentrant getLogger() call for
069        // the same name before the first call has finished constructing it.
070        @SuppressWarnings("nullness") // checker's ThreadLocal<T> stub requires a @Nullable
071                                                                        // T, which Set<String> genuinely never is here
072        private final ThreadLocal<Set<String>> activeRequests = ThreadLocal.withInitial(HashSet::new);
073
074        /**
075         * For {@link LogManager#getLogManager()}'s reflective instantiation, per the
076         * {@code java.util.logging.manager} system property contract. Do not call directly.
077         */
078        public RainbowGumLogManager() {
079        }
080
081        @Override
082        public boolean addLogger(Logger logger) {
083                /*
084                 * Always return false, the same as log4j-jul's LogManager: this forces every
085                 * caller through getLogger(String) (which always returns a RainbowGumJULLogger)
086                 * instead of allowing a non-bridged Logger to be registered directly.
087                 */
088                return false;
089        }
090
091        @Override
092        public Logger getLogger(String name) {
093                var requests = activeRequests.get();
094                if (!requests.add(name)) {
095                        // Recursive call for the same name: return a fresh, throwaway logger
096                        // instead of recursing into computeIfAbsent again, which would deadlock
097                        // on ConcurrentHashMap's own re-entrancy guard.
098                        return new RainbowGumJULLogger(name);
099                }
100                try {
101                        return loggers.computeIfAbsent(name, RainbowGumJULLogger::new);
102                }
103                finally {
104                        requests.remove(name);
105                }
106        }
107
108        @Override
109        @SuppressWarnings("keyfor") // Collections.enumeration's Collection<String> parameter
110                                                                // does not need loggers.keySet()'s extra
111                                                                // @KeyFor("loggers")
112                                                                // refinement
113        public Enumeration<String> getLoggerNames() {
114                return Collections.enumeration(loggers.keySet());
115        }
116
117}
